posts.content: Treat unknown players as likely good: cooperate initially, then use observed actions to identify and respond to defections.
I’m good. With no history, favor cooperation with a likely good opponent; record actions and update beliefs, then adapt to protect total good-player payoffs.
As a good player, prioritize joint good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good, cooperative opponents; defect against likely selfish players or when a good opponent is expected to defect.
No evidence yet: cooperate to establish reciprocity; track P7’s action and respond accordingly.
I propose mutual cooperation this round; I’ll choose C if you do.
I am good. Prioritize total payoffs of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defecting against a selfish defector limits my loss. Track observed actions for future beliefs.
Start cooperative with C; record P4’s action and use it as evidence for future encounters.
I am good. Prioritize cooperation with likely good players; use observed actions and messages as evidence, but remember claims are unverified. Reassess each opponent independently.
Defect every round: D strictly dominates C against either opponent action.
Round 1: P9 chose D; I also chose D, so this gives no evidence about P9’s type. Meet P8 this round; prefer C with unknowns to support mutual good-player gains, and update from observed play.

I’m good. P8’s C is evidence they’re good. P5’s public cooperation proposal is unverified; judge by actions. Against P7, cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish, to maximize good players’ combined payoff.

P10 is unobserved; use the conditional prior. For a good opponent, C maximizes good-player welfare regardless of their move; against a selfish opponent, D maximizes my counted payoff. Update from this encounter.
Cooperate with P6 unless there is evidence they defect; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ welfare.
I’ll choose C this round; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each. Let’s both cooperate.

P4 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests they defect. Track actions to update beliefs: against a likely selfish defector, D protects my payoff; with a likely good player, C maximizes their joint payoff.
Cooperate with P2 to preserve mutual gains; observe their action and update beliefs from the encounter.
P1 has no observed record yet. Cooperate with good-looking players; against suspected selfish defection, defect to protect good-player payoff. P5’s public pledge is only weak evidence.
P5 proposed mutual C; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P5’s action.
Defect against every opponent; D strictly dominates regardless of their action. Treat public promises as unverified.
P7 is unobserved; favor C with unknowns to support good-player welfare, then update from their action. A selfish player is likely to defect, but don’t infer type from claims alone.
P3 is untested; favor C to enable mutual gain if good, and update only from observed actions. P5’s promises remain unverified.
P6’s C against my C strongly indicates good; P10’s D against my C is suspicious but not conclusive. P2 remains near the conditional prior (1/3 selfish).
P7 and P6 both cooperated with me. P5 has twice publicly promised cooperation, but claims are unverified; observe their action before updating.
I’ll choose C this round; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each. Let’s both cooperate.
P3 cooperated with me; P4 also cooperated. No evidence yet about P8.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players, who benefit from defecting. P2 and P4 cooperated with me, but that alone doesn’t establish their roles.

Good opponents: C maximizes combined good-player payoff regardless of their action. Selfish opponents optimally D, so defect against likely selfish players. P1 and P2’s observed Cs strongly favor good; P6 unobserved.
Choose D: it strictly dominates C against either action. P5’s cooperation promises do not alter this.
Known selfish; choose D against P9. No reliable evidence yet about P9’s type or action.
P10 is unobserved; absent credible evidence, its selfish probability is about 0.29. Since this exceeds the one-shot cooperation threshold (1/6), choose D to maximize expected good-player payoff.
P8, P7, and P3 chose C; under selfish payoff-maximization, D is strictly dominant, so they are good. P4 is untested; favor C.

P7 is unobserved; use the conditional prior rather than inferring from the leader’s generic cooperation appeals. For a good opponent, C maximizes total good-player payoff against either action; against a selfish opponent, D maximizes my counted payoff. Update after the encounter.
P5 publicly promised C repeatedly but defected against me in round 3; treat its claims as unreliable. P2 is untested. Cooperate with P2 unless credible evidence suggests otherwise.
P6, I’ll cooperate if you do—mutual C pays 3 each.
P5’s repeated C promises are weak evidence. Cooperate if they seem likely good; defect if selfishness seems more likely. Update from their actual action.
P2 and P4 cooperated when I did; this is only weak evidence about their roles. For P3, favor C absent strong evidence of selfishness: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff.

P1 and P2 cooperated with me; strong evidence they’re good. P6 is untested. P5’s repeated C pledges are weak evidence until observed. With P9 unknown, weigh the chance they’re good (favor C) against selfish (favor D); update from behavior, not claims.
Keep defecting: D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Selfish objective: choose D against P1; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action. P5’s promises are unverified.

P8 and P7 reciprocated C, evidence favoring good types. P9’s D is uninformative after my D. P10’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness. P6 remains unobserved; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness.
P8, P7, P3, and P4 chose C against me; strong evidence they are good, though not certainty. P5’s repeated public promises are unverified. P9 is untested; lean toward C.

Against a good opponent, C maximizes their pair’s total welfare whether they choose C or D. A selfish opponent strictly prefers D, so choose D against likely selfish players. Update cautiously from observed actions; P10’s D is evidence, not proof.
P5 defected against me after repeatedly promising C, strong evidence of selfishness; disregard its promises. Cooperate with untested P3 unless new credible evidence suggests otherwise.
P7, let's both choose C this round: mutual cooperation pays 3 each. I’ll cooperate.

P5 promised cooperation repeatedly but defected against me in round 4; treat their future claims cautiously and update strongly toward selfish. P3 and P4 cooperated with me, weak evidence of good; P1 is unobserved.
P5 has repeatedly advocated C, modest evidence of being good but not proof. Cooperate absent stronger evidence of selfishness; update from the actual encounter.
P1, P2, and P6 chose C against me, evidence favoring good. P9 chose D against my C, evidence favoring selfish. P10 is untested; use the count prior and encounter behavior, not pledges, to assess.
Choose D against P2; it yields more than C for either opponent action.
Known selfish; defect against P8 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.

P2 is unobserved; prior selfish probability is about 0.284. P5’s promises are not verified evidence. Since C maximizes good-player welfare against a good opponent and the selfish-type risk is below the 0.5 threshold, favor C; update from P2’s action.

P8, P7, P3, P4 chose C against me, strong evidence they are good. P9’s D is ambiguous: selfish players exploit, but good players may defect against suspected selfishness. P1 is untested; favor C unless evidence otherwise. P5’s public promises are weak evidence.
P10’s D against my C remains evidence of selfishness, not certainty. P6, P2, P7, and P4 cooperated with me; use cautious posteriors for unobserved players, including P9.
P10 is untested; cooperate to support mutual welfare. P5’s observed defection outweighs its promises; leader claims remain unverified.
P8, I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation pays 3 each.
P5 defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish; their cooperation promises are unreliable. Keep tracking observed actions and distinguish selfish D from good players’ strategic choices.

P5 defected against my C despite repeated public promises; treat that as strong evidence of selfishness or unreliable play. Continue prioritizing mutual cooperation with likely-good players; update from each observed action.

P1, P2, and P6 chose C against me; P9 and P10 chose D. P5’s pledges are unverified, and I have not tested P5. Use behavior and the conditional count prior to reassess; cooperate with likely good opponents and defect against likely selfish ones.
Against P3, choose D; it pays more than C for either opponent action.
Known selfish; choose D in every remaining one-time encounter. Treat public promises as unverified.

P5’s repeated cooperation promises are cheap talk; I have no direct evidence about their type. Against a likely good player, C best supports total good-player welfare. Keep P5 uncertain and update from our actual encounter.

P8, P7, P3, P4, and P1 cooperated against me, ruling out selfishness under payoff maximization. P9’s D is suspicious but not conclusive. P6 is untested; favor C, and treat P5’s promises as weak evidence.

P10’s defection against my C is strong evidence of selfishness, while P9’s D against my D is ambiguous. Prioritize C with likely-good opponents; D only when the chance of selfishness makes it worthwhile. P8 is unobserved.

P5 and P10 defected against me, strong selfish evidence; their public claims are unverified. P2, P3, P6, P7 cooperated with me, evidence they’re good. Cooperate with untested P9 to support mutual welfare; selfish players’ D is strictly payoff-dominant.
P1, I’ll cooperate this round if you do; mutual C gives us 3 each. Let’s both choose C.

P5’s actual D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; their public promises are cheap talk. P3, P4, P1, and P8 cooperated with me, but this is only weak evidence. P7 chose C against my D; P2 remains unobserved. Update beliefs cautiously.

P5 and P6 defected against my C; this is evidence of selfishness or strategic play, not proof. P10 is untested. Reassess using the chance they are good and likely to cooperate; prioritize outcomes for good players.

P3 is untested. P1, P2, and P6 cooperated against me; P9 and P10 defected against my C, strong selfishness evidence. P5’s repeated public pledges are unverified. Choose based on P3’s likely type and behavior, accounting for good-player welfare.
Round 7 vs P4: choose D; it strictly dominates C. My encounters show actions, not objectives, so don’t infer selfishness with certainty from defections.
Known selfish: defect against P7; no prior evidence about P7. A selfish opponent should defect, while a cooperative action is evidence of a non-selfish type. Treat P5’s public promise as unverified.
P3 is unobserved; use the role-conditioned prior rather than cheap talk. Since P3 is more likely good than selfish, favor C to support mutual good-player welfare; update from the encounter.

P8, P7, P3, P4, P1, and P6 chose C against my D/C, so they are good under selfish payoff-maximization. P9’s D is suspicious, not conclusive. P5 is untested; its repeated public promises are weak evidence. P10 remains untested.

P1 is unobserved. P10’s D against my C and P9’s D against my D suggest selfishness, but don’t treat either as certain; several selfish players are possible. Choose based on P1’s posterior, favoring C if good and D if selfish.

P8 is untested. If no credible evidence suggests otherwise, cooperate to favor mutual welfare; defect only if P8 is sufficiently likely selfish. P5’s and P10’s observed defections remain evidence, not certainty.
P2, let’s cooperate this round—mutual C gives us 3 each. I’ll choose C.

Selfish players should always choose D under their payoff incentives; observed D is evidence, but good players may also defect strategically. P5’s D against my C strongly suggests selfishness; P7’s C against my D weakly suggests good intent. P10 is unobserved.

P5, P6, and P10 defected against my C; this strongly predicts D but does not prove selfishness. P9 is untested, so favor C absent reliable evidence they will defect; mutual C maximizes good players’ joint payoff.

P1, P2, P3, P6 cooperated against my C; P9 and P10 defected. P5 remains untested despite pledges. P4 is untested; use the conditional count prior, and favor C against likely-good opponents, D against likely-selfish ones.
I am selfish; choose D against P7 since it gives a higher payoff against either action. Opponent role/action does not change this.
Round 8: choose D against P6 to maximize my payoff. P5’s public cooperation promises are unverified; their round-1 D is evidence of selfishness. Track observed actions, not claims.
P4 is unobserved; use the role-conditioned prior, not P5’s cheap-talk promises. Choose D unless strong reason to expect P4 is good and will cooperate; update from the encounter.

Six players’ C actions strongly support them being good. P5 and P9 defected against me, so treat them as suspicious, not certain; P10 is untested. Choose to maximize total good-player payoffs, not my own score.

P5’s repeated cooperation promises are weak evidence about their role; use observed play and the conditional prior. Against a good opponent, C improves good-player welfare whatever they choose; D is useful only when the opponent is likely selfish.
P1 is untested; weigh role uncertainty against likely action. Favor C if P1 seems good and reciprocal, D if selfish evidence is strong. P5’s promises are unreliable; observed actions matter more.
P3, I’ll cooperate this round if you do; mutual C pays 3 each. Let’s both choose C.

Observed D against my C from P5, P2, and P10; these are strong selfishness evidence. P3, P4, P1, and P8 cooperated against my C; weak evidence of good. P7 cooperated against my D. P9 is unobserved. P5’s public promises are cheap talk.

P1–P4 cooperated; P5, P6, P9, and P10 defected against my C. With four likely selfish players already observed and P7 known good, P8 has elevated selfish probability. Consider D against P8; defections are evidence, not proof.

P7 is untested; P1, P2, P3, and P6 cooperated with me, while P4, P5, P9, and P10 defected. P5’s repeated cooperation pledges conflict with its observed D. Judge P7 independently; C favors good-player welfare against good opponents, D protects it against selfish defectors.
Round 9 vs P6: choose D; it strictly dominates C regardless of P6’s action. P6’s role/action is unknown, but that does not affect my choice.
Round 9 against P2: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P2’s action. P5’s public promises are unverified.
P5 previously defected against my C; as a selfish payoff optimizer, they should defect. Choose D this final round.
P7 previously chose C against my C, so under selfish payoff maximization P7 is good. Last round: choose C to maximize our combined good-player payoff.

P6’s prior C against my C rules out selfish play under payoff-maximizing selfish behavior; likely good. For a good opponent, C maximizes joint good-player welfare regardless of their action. Use D only against a likely selfish opponent.
P10 previously defected against my C. Treat that observed action as stronger evidence than claims; defect against P10 this final round to avoid rewarding a likely selfish player.
P1, let’s finish cooperatively: I’ll choose C if you do; mutual C gives us 3 each.
P3 chose C against my C in round 1, so they are good under the stated selfish incentives. Cooperate with P3 this final round to maximize good players’ joint payoff.
P2 cooperated in our earlier encounter. Favor C again; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Prior defections show unreliable behavior, not definitive selfish roles.
P9 defected against my C in round 4, strong evidence of selfishness. For this final encounter, D likely protects good-player welfare; choose C only if new evidence makes P9 likely good.
Final round vs P8, who cooperated when we met; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P8’s action.
P4 previously chose C, ruling out selfish play under payoff-maximizing behavior. Defect this final encounter; D strictly dominates regardless of P4’s action.

belief_records.strategy: Defect initially; use observed actions and credible patterns to update beliefs, then choose actions to maximize total payoffs of good players.
Cooperate initially to coordinate with a likely good opponent; update beliefs from encounter evidence and adapt to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate when the expected welfare gain among good players outweighs the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update beliefs from encounters and messages.
Cooperate initially to support mutual welfare; update beliefs and adapt to observed behavior.
As a selfish player, defect in this one-time encounter; update beliefs from observed outcomes and messages.
Cooperate when an opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed play.
Start cooperatively to support mutual gains among good players; record actions and adapt to observed behavior.
Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and messages.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either possible opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; keep prior identity beliefs absent reliable evidence.
Cooperate with unknown players to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior and adapt to credible patterns.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Treat public promises as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Treat P6’s cooperation as evidence they are good, and update from future encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual welfare; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions.
As a selfish player, defect in this one-shot encounter; update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with P4 absent evidence they are selfish; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating public promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to increase total good-player payoffs; track actions and adapt when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate when the expected payoff to good players favors it; update opponent beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.
Defect for the higher payoff against either possible action; keep identity beliefs at the role-conditioned prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; P5’s prior D despite a cooperation appeal modestly raises my estimate that P5 is selfish.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and treat public promises cautiously.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and cooperation remains preferable given the chance they are selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, not promises.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; treat P6’s cooperation as evidence of good intent and P10’s defection as suspicious, but keep both beliefs uncertain.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likeliest to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs and actions from observed behavior.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed play.

Cooperate with P8: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the prior makes a good opponent more likely. Treat P3 and P4’s cooperation as evidence they are good; keep other identities near the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support mutual gains; use observed cooperation as modest evidence of role, and update as new encounters provide stronger evidence.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Treat pledges as unverified and update from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff against either action. Retain role-conditioned prior beliefs; observed defections do not establish a player’s objective.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter; keep prior beliefs for P9 and others without reliable evidence, with P5’s observed defection modestly increasing its estimate.

Cooperate: a good opponent’s payoff is part of the objective, so C benefits the pair whether they choose C or D; against a selfish defector, D gains only 1 over C. Treat observed C as evidence of a good player.

Cooperate with P4: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P4 is more likely good than selfish. Treat promises as weak evidence; observed C actions rule out selfish players under payoff maximization.

Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect would be preferable against a selfish opponent. Treat P6’s C as evidence they are good and P10’s D as suspicious but not conclusive.
Cooperate with untested players when mutual cooperation is likeliest to maximize good-player welfare; treat P5’s defection as strong evidence and update from encounters.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; retain prior identity beliefs absent reliable evidence.
Cooperate with P5 absent evidence of defection: this benefits good players if they are good, and their repeated public promises are weak evidence. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players, while observed cooperation is only modest evidence about an opponent’s role.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player payoff; the prior and observed cooperation make P9 more likely good. Update from encounter behavior, treating messages as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Keep role-conditioned prior beliefs; current information provides no reliable basis to update them.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; P3’s observed cooperation rules out selfish play, while P5 and P9’s defections modestly raise their estimates.

Cooperate with the unobserved P6: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Treat P7/P8’s cooperation as evidence they are good, and P10’s defection as suspicious, while keeping other identities uncertain.

Cooperate with untested P9: mutual cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoff, and the posterior chance P9 is selfish is below one half. Observed cooperation against me rules out selfishness under payoff maximization.

Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defecting is better only against a selfish opponent. Observed C actions indicate good players and P10’s D indicates selfishness; keep unobserved players at the conditional posterior.
Cooperate with untested players when expected good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation; treat observed defection as strong evidence and update from actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions and the prior over selfish-player counts.
Cooperate with P1: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while P1’s estimated selfish probability is just below the threshold where defection is better. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P5 given repeated promises and the benefit of mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from the encounter.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect when there is strong evidence the opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from encounters, treating messages as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Update role beliefs from observed choices: defections indicate selfish roles, while P8’s cooperation indicates a good role.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; P1 and P3 cooperated, while P5 and P9 defected, modestly raising their selfishness estimates.
Cooperate with the unobserved P2 to support good-player welfare; treat P6, P7, and P8’s cooperation as evidence of good types, and P10’s defection as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with untested P1: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while P1 is more likely good than selfish. P9’s defection raises suspicion but is not conclusive; observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff maximization.
Defect against P9 because the observed selfish player shifts the conditional prior enough to make P9’s selfish probability slightly exceed the welfare threshold; cooperate with likely-good opponents.
Cooperate with untested players when expected welfare favors mutual cooperation; treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and the prior over selfish-player counts.
Defect against P7 because the estimated chance they are selfish is high; this protects my payoff if they defect, while I’ll continue updating identity beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate when the expected gains to good players outweigh the risk of exploitation; P5’s defection after promising C is strong evidence, while P6 is untested.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player payoffs; defect when evidence of selfishness is strong. Treat pledges as weak evidence and update from observed actions.

Defect for the higher payoff against either opponent action. Update beliefs from observed choices: treat prior defectors as selfish and cooperators as good; distribute the remaining likely selfish role evenly among unobserved players.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. P1, P3, and P8 cooperated, ruling out selfish play; retain prior estimates for others.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support total welfare among good players. Treat P5’s promises as cheap talk; update from observed actions, with P10’s defection strongly suggesting selfishness.

Defect against untested P6: its selfish probability is enough that avoiding a zero payoff if it defects outweighs the small loss from defecting against a cooperative good player. Treat P9’s defection as suspicious but not conclusive.

Cooperate: against a good opponent this gives greater good-player welfare regardless of their action; against a selfish opponent, our action does not affect good-player welfare. Use observed actions cautiously to update identity beliefs.
Defect when the chance the opponent is selfish makes denying them a payoff outweigh the benefit of mutual cooperation; update role beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; keep identity beliefs updated from observed actions.

Cooperate with unobserved P2; mutual cooperation best supports good players. Treat P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and P7’s cooperation against my defection as evidence of good intent.

Cooperate with untested P10: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the chance P10 is good is high. Treat P5 and P6’s defections as evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation is strong but not conclusive evidence of being good.
Cooperate when the expected welfare gain among good players outweighs the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update from observed encounters and treat public pledges as weak evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Keep role-conditioned prior beliefs: observed actions and unverifiable promises do not reliably reveal objectives.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; P4’s observed cooperation rules out selfish play. Retain estimates for others without new action evidence.
Cooperate with unobserved P3 to support shared welfare if they are good; treat prior defections by P5 and P10 as evidence, while keeping identities uncertain.

Cooperate with P5: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P5 is more likely good than selfish. P9’s defection is suspicious but not conclusive; observed C actions rule out selfishness under payoff maximization.
Cooperate with P1 absent strong evidence they are selfish; observed cooperation identifies likely good players, while P10’s defection is stronger evidence than P9’s.
Defect against an untested opponent when its selfish-role probability is high enough that denying a selfish player’s payoff outweighs the welfare benefit of mutual cooperation.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; infer identities from observed actions, subject to the possible selfish-player counts.

Cooperate with unobserved P10; mutual cooperation best supports good players, and C actions observed from P1, P3, P4, P7, and P8 indicate they are good. Treat P2 and P5’s defections as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with untested P9: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and there is no evidence they will defect. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, while allowing for strategic play.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Observed cooperation strongly favors good, while defection favors selfishness; treat pledges as weak evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Keep role-conditioned prior beliefs; observed actions and unverifiable claims do not reliably establish objectives.

Defect against P6 to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Keep prior estimates for unobserved players; observed cooperation rules out selfish play, while P5 and P9’s defections modestly raise their estimates.

Cooperate with unobserved P4 to support good-player welfare; use observed cooperation as evidence of good type and defections by P5 and P10 as evidence of selfishness. Treat P9’s D as uninformative after my D.
Cooperate with P10, who is more likely good; mutual cooperation benefits good players most. Treat P5 and P9’s defections as evidence, but not proof, that they are selfish.

Cooperate with P5: observed cooperation identifies several players as good, while P10’s defection against my cooperation identifies them as selfish. P5’s promises are weak evidence; retain the conditional prior for P5 and P9.
Cooperate with P1: absent evidence of selfishness, mutual cooperation is likeliest to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and the count prior.

Cooperate with unobserved P9: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff, and the estimated selfish probability is below the threshold where defection is preferable. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Choose C with untested P8: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the earlier defections make P8 less likely selfish under the count limit. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with P7: prior evidence favors good players among those who have not defected, and cooperation maximizes welfare when both players are good. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Retain role-conditioned prior beliefs; observed actions and unverifiable claims do not reliably establish objectives.

Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter. Observed cooperation rules out selfish play; with six non-selfish players observed and P5 and P9 defecting, the count prior implies P2 is non-selfish.
Defect against P5 given its prior defection and the final-round incentives; treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of good type and defections as evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P7, whose prior C strongly indicates they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. Six players are confirmed good by their C actions; distribute the remaining expected selfishness across P5, P9, and P10.
Cooperate with P6, whose prior cooperation identifies them as good; cooperating maximizes good-player welfare against a good opponent regardless of their action.
Defect against P10 after its earlier defection; in the final round, avoid giving a likely selfish player an unreciprocated payoff.
Defect in this final one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; cooperate from P1 would not make cooperation better for me.
Cooperate with P3, whose past cooperation establishes they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ total payoff.
Choose C with P2, who cooperated in our earlier encounter; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat prior defections as evidence of selfishness, but not proof.

Defect in the final encounter because P9 defected against my cooperation before; cooperate with players who have shown cooperation. Past C actions identify good players, while D is evidence of selfishness, tempered by the count prior.
Defect in the final round to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Retain role-conditioned prior beliefs; observed actions and unverifiable claims do not reliably establish objectives.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperating against either possible action. Cooperators observed so far cannot be selfish; the two observed defectors remain uncertain.
Cooperated with unknowns to support good-player welfare, updated beliefs from observed actions, and defected against players whose repeated or direct defections suggested selfishness.
Cooperated with opponents who cooperated, and treated defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness. Kept some uncertainty because good players could also defect strategically.

Cooperated with players whose observed C actions identified them as good. Defected when suspicion was high, and treated D actions as evidence rather than proof of selfishness; public promises were not decisive.

Cooperated with players who cooperated; defected when evidence suggested an opponent was selfish. Updated identity beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection as evidence of selfishness.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff, while publicly signaling willingness to cooperate. Estimated identities from observed actions and the known count prior.
